entries.name: DARPA — Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency
entries.observes: Whether any quantum computing approach can achieve utility-scale operation — computational value exceeding cost — by 2033, via the QBI three-stage evaluation (Stage A concept characterization; Stage B yearlong R&D-plan and risk-mitigation scrutiny; Stage C government verification-and-validation of a constructed-and-operated system). US2QC was the pilot effort folded into QBI.

programs.name: US2QC
programs.detail: Pilot: Atom Computing, Microsoft, PsiQuantum; final phase ≡ QBI Stage C goals.

programs.name: QBI
programs.detail: 18 companies entered Stage A; 11 advanced to Stage B on 2025-11-06; Google Quantum AI joined Stage A Sep 2025.

entries.note: Selection to a stage is an evaluation event, not a passed test. QBI is explicitly not a winner-picking competition.

entries.name: NQCC — UK National Quantum Computing Centre
entries.observes: Hands-on test and validation of vendor systems installed under the Quantum Computing Testbed Programme, and mapping of real-world applications onto each architecture.

programs.name: Quantum Computing Testbed Programme
programs.detail: £30M with UKRI/Innovate UK; seven testbeds contracted for deployment at Harwell Campus by March 2025.

entries.note: Accepting an installation begins the evaluation; it does not conclude it.

entries.name: UKRI / Innovate UK — Technology Missions Fund
entries.observes: Competition awards and milestone-based SBRI funding for the seven NQCC testbeds.

programs.name: SBRI Quantum Testbed Competition
programs.detail: Aegiq, Infleqtion (Cold Quanta UK), ORCA Computing, Oxford Ionics, Rigetti UK, Quantum Motion, QuEra.

entries.note: An award is funding plus a delivery contract — not evidence the delivered system performs.

entries.name: US DOE / SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
entries.observes: Hosts and exercises PsiQuantum's largest cryogenic module for on-site testing.
entries.note: Hosting a module under test is infrastructure participation, not endorsement of results.

entries.name: Illinois Quantum & Microelectronics Park / Quantum Proving Ground
entries.observes: Physical site for utility-scale deployment: PsiQuantum's Chicago Quantum Compute Center and DARPA's proving-ground presence.
entries.note: State-backed capacity commitment; a site under construction is not a working machine.

entries.name: QED-C — Quantum Economic Development Consortium
entries.observes: Supply-chain maturity, benchmarking taxonomy, standards and workforce metrics across member companies.
entries.note: Industry consortium; its metrics describe the field, membership describes a mailing list.

entries.name: NPL — UK National Physical Laboratory
entries.observes: Measurement standards and independent characterisation capability underpinning quantum device claims.
entries.note: Metrology capacity exists; no Genesis evidence entry is yet measured by NPL.

entries.name: Metriq (Unitary Foundation)
entries.observes: Published benchmark submissions and cross-platform comparability of reported quantum-computing metrics.
entries.note: Aggregation of published results; comparability is limited by heterogeneous methods.

entries.name: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking
entries.observes: Procurement and hosting of European quantum systems; demand-side signal across architectures.
entries.note: A purchase order proves a buyer decided; it does not prove the machine works at utility scale.
